clue.text: Sylph-like being? That's fanciful

definitions.meaning: a light, airy sprite of the fairy kind
impractical and whimsical, the idiomatic sense of the hyphenated phrase

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase names an ethereal sprite; as an idiom it means vague and impractical, a synonym for fanciful.

clue.text: Advantage of a disguise, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly tells us the words are heard rather than seen, so we go by their sound

parts.note: a disguise is a veil, giving A VEIL

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what is gained by wearing a disguise, according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' marks the homophone: A VEIL, said aloud, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, avail means use or benefit, as in 'to no avail', a synonym for advantage.

clue.text: Extremely rare flower — perennial?

indicators.note: taking the word rare to its extremes leaves only its first and last letters

parts.note: a flower here is something that flows, such as a current of water

explanation.surface: A gardener asks whether an unusual bloom will come back every year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is the classic crossword trick: not a bloom but a thing that flows, a CURRENT. 'Extremely' takes the first and last letters of rare, RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perennial keeps coming back year after year, just as a recurrent thing happens repeatedly.

clue.text: Instruments George allows after Alfred turns up

indicators.note: after places the George and allows pieces behind the turned Alfred
in a down clue, turning up means the name reads from the bottom to the top

parts.note: Alf is the short form of the name Alfred
Geo is an abbreviation for the name George
lets means allows, as in permits

explanation.surface: Musical instruments are permitted by George once Alfred finally shows up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' works because this is a down entry, so the reversed name reads upwards; 'after' places the rest behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Flageolets are small whistle-like woodwind instruments, so they are examples of instruments.

clue.text: Climbers crossing outer bounds — they may be tickled

indicators.note: the climbing plants cross over, that is enclose, the other piece

parts.note: ivies are climbing plants

indicators.note: the bounds of the word outer are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Climbing plants grow across the edges of something that might be tickled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bounds' supplies the first and last letters of outer, and 'crossing' sets them inside the climbers. Pianists are said to tickle the ivories.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano keys are called ivories, and playing the piano is jokily called tickling the ivories, an idiom.

clue.text: In Mexico, peninsula having whip-round for foreign currency? On the contrary

indicators.note: round would normally put the whip around the money, but the tail of the clue reverses that
On the contrary says swap the roles, so the currency goes round the whip instead

parts.note: the yuan is the currency of China
a cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip

explanation.surface: A Mexican region is said to pass the hat round for foreign money, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: A whip-round is a collection of money, a decoy; the parse uses 'whip' and 'round' separately, and 'On the contrary' makes the money go round the whip.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yucatan is a large peninsula in south-east Mexico, separating the Gulf of Mexico from the Caribbean.

clue.text: It's invigorating to catch king out

indicators.note: out says the king is taken away from the word for catch

parts.note: to nick is to catch, as police nick a criminal
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Seizing a monarch and throwing him out is a refreshing experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes the king from the word for catch; 'to' stays as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is something that refreshes or restores vigour, so it is a thing that invigorates.

clue.text: Drink left for duck

parts.note: tea is a drink

explanation.surface: A drink is left out for a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: The teal is a small freshwater duck, so it is an example of a duck.

clue.text: Seen in Tuscany — a large antelope

indicators.note: the answer can be seen inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A big antelope is spotted in the Italian countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned antelope of southern Africa.

clue.text: Is it possible for sounds on tip of tongue to constitute language?

parts.note: can asks whether something is possible
tones are sounds

indicators.note: the tip here is the far end of the word tongue, its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether noises made with the tongue can count as a language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip of' takes the last letter of tongue, E; 'on' is a link, the sounds sitting on the tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantonese is the Chinese language spoken in Guangdong and Hong Kong, an example of a language.

clue.text: Twin Cities captured by first-rate artist? That's capital

indicators.note: captured by means the cities are held inside the other pieces

parts.note: A, as in A1 or grade A, means first-rate
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist
C is an abbreviation for city, so two of them give CC

explanation.surface: Minneapolis and St Paul are taken over by a top painter, which is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: The Twin Cities suggests Minneapolis and St Paul, but here it is just two city abbreviations, which 'captured by' puts inside the first-rate artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital city of Ghana, so it is an example of a capital.

clue.text: Another time, another age — an icon

indicators.note: another signals that the following letters are made into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A fresh era comes round, with a new idol for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' rearranges AGE and AN ICON together.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means on a further occasion, a repeat, which is what another time means.

clue.text: Force enlists car thieves

indicators.note: to force letters is to wrench them into a new order

explanation.surface: The police take on staff to deal with car thieves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' looks like a police force but is the anagram signal for ENLISTS CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is theft, so larcenists are those who commit it: thieves.

clue.text: Texas city without any chiefs or leaders

indicators.note: leaders are the opening letters of each of the words before

explanation.surface: A town in Texas is said to have no bosses or heads at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes the first letters of without, any, chiefs, or.
explanation.definitionFit: Waco is a city in central Texas, known for the 1993 siege there.

clue.text: Bird that's underweight, for example, raised a monument

parts.note: read as under weight: the bird goes beneath a weight, the stone of fourteen pounds
a hen is a bird

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters read upwards

explanation.surface: A skinny bird raised a memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underweight' splits into under weight: in a down entry the bird sits below the stone, a British weight of 14 pounds. 'raised' turns the example abbreviation upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonehenge is the prehistoric stone circle on Salisbury Plain in England, a famous ancient monument.

clue.text: Narks, being redundant, tail off

indicators.note: tail off cuts the final letter from the word that came before

parts.note: needless means redundant, unnecessary

explanation.surface: Informers lose their jobs and fade away.
explanation.walkthrough: Narks looks like the noun for informers, but it is a verb: annoys. 'tail off' drops the last S of NEEDLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To nark someone is British slang for irritating them, just as to needle someone is to provoke them.

clue.text: A letter from Greece (one teachers write about) that's radioactive

indicators.note: about turns the whole string of pieces back to front

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
I is the Roman numeral one
the NUT is the National Union of Teachers in Britain
to pen is to write

explanation.surface: A Greek letter about a teaching union turns out to be dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses MU I NUT PEN as one run. The NUT is the British National Union of Teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptunium is a radioactive metallic element, number 93, so it is something radioactive.

clue.text: Striking back on board

indicators.note: back signals that the little word beside it is read backwards

parts.note: a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: Hitting back while aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the little word round before the board is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Notable means remarkable or noteworthy, a synonym for striking in its sense of eye-catching.

clue.text: Emperor, for the good of his country, isolated on Elba initially

parts.note: his country is France, where good is bon
apart means set aside or isolated

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of Elba

explanation.surface: An emperor, for the good of France, was exiled on Elba at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his country' is Napoleon's France, so good is the French BON. 'initially' gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of the French in 1804.

clue.text: The worst and the best occasion for quick service?

parts.note: the pits is slang for the worst
the top is the best

explanation.surface: Something is both dreadful and excellent, ideal for fast attention.
explanation.walkthrough: In motor racing, a pit stop is a quick halt for fuel and tyres.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit stop is a brief halt for fast refuelling and repairs, so it is an occasion for quick service.

clue.text: Empty pews? Revise hymn book!

indicators.note: an empty word loses its insides, keeping only first and last letters

parts.note: to alter is to revise

explanation.surface: Churchgoers have gone, so the hymnals should be updated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' leaves the first and last letters of pews, PS. Revise is a decoy anagram signal; here it simply means ALTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalter is a book of psalms, the hymns of the Bible, so it is a kind of hymn book.

clue.text: Can fine involve money?

indicators.note: to involve in its old sense is to twist or wind up, so the letters are twisted

explanation.surface: A question asks whether a penalty might involve cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involve' signals a rearrangement of CAN FINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Finance means funds or money, as in raising finance for a project.

clue.text: Plant producing horse-drawn vehicles

parts.note: a fly is a light horse-drawn carriage
a trap is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: A factory turns out horse-drawn carriages.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant looks like a factory, but it is the vegetable kind: the Venus flytrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A flytrap is a carnivorous plant that catches insects, such as the Venus flytrap.

clue.text: Press used by Turgenev

indicators.note: used by means the answer is borrowed from within the author's name

explanation.surface: A printing press is used by a Russian novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge is to press, in the sense of strongly encouraging.

clue.text: Guardian leaders — reticent or effusive?

indicators.note: leaders, plural, takes the leading pair of letters of Guardian

parts.note: shy means reticent

explanation.surface: A newspaper's editorials are asked whether they are reserved or gushing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' here is the first two letters of Guardian, GU; leaders are also newspaper editorials, the decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Gushy means overly enthusiastic and sentimental, a synonym for effusive.

clue.text: Woman taking man to ecclesiastical limits in section of church

parts.note: a lady is a woman
a chap is a man

indicators.note: the limits of the word ecclesiastical are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A woman leads a man to the edge of church affairs, in a part of the building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits' gives the first and last letters of ecclesiastical, EL.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady chapel is a chapel dedicated to the Virgin Mary within a larger church.

clue.text: Hark, we hear the composer

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by its sound alone

parts.note: list is an old word for listen, an imperative like hark

explanation.surface: Listen, the composer is coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' marks the homophone: LIST, an archaic word for listen, sounds like the composer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a nineteenth-century Hungarian composer and piano virtuoso.

clue.text: Beloved band's last audience

indicators.note: last picks out the final letter of the word band

parts.note: an ear is a hearing, an audience, as in gaining someone's ear

explanation.surface: A favourite group plays its final audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' takes D from band; an audience is a hearing, so EAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear means beloved, as in a dear friend.

clue.text: One may examine tickets for theatrical caller

definitions.meaning: a ticket checker on a bus or train
the visitor in Priestley's play An ... Calls

explanation.walkthrough: An Inspector Calls is a well-known play by J. B. Priestley.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticket checker is called by this title, and Priestley's play features one who calls on a family.

clue.text: Fates familiar to Scandinavians and one or two Poles?

parts.note: one of the Poles, north, gives N
the two poles north and south give N and S

explanation.surface: Destinies known in Scandinavia, and to a Pole or two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one or two Poles' reads as one pole, N, then OR, then two poles, N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse mythology the Norns are the three goddesses who shape destiny, the Scandinavian Fates.

clue.text: Chief magistrate provides sauce recipe

parts.note: mayo is short for mayonnaise, a sauce
R abbreviates recipe, from Latin recipe, take

explanation.surface: A head official supplies instructions for a sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: R for recipe is the prescription abbreviation, from Latin for 'take'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayor is the head of a town council and historically its chief magistrate.

clue.text: Stand for 50% more here

indicators.note: 50% means half of the following word, here its latter half

parts.note: present means here, in attendance

explanation.surface: Agree to an increase of half here.
explanation.walkthrough: '50%' takes the second half of more, RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent something is to stand for it, as a symbol does.
